content_units: 90-Minute Game Night Lineup

A simple, low-mess plan for   6 adults + 2 kids (10 and 12)   using fast-to-learn party games with no app required. This order starts high-energy, shifts into creative teamwork, and finishes with the most social bluffing game.
Recommended Game Order
Order   Game   Type   Estimated Time   Why it fits this group
1     Just One     Word game   20 min   Easy warm-up, cooperative, very kid-friendly
2     Telestrations     Drawing game   30 min   Big laughs, simple rules, low pressure
3     Werewords Deluxe   or   One Night Ultimate Werewolf     Bluffing / deduction   35 min   Strong finish with more tension and table talk
4     Wrap-up buffer     Score reset / snack / stretch   5 min   Keeps the night on time without feeling rushed
Game-by-Game Host Plan
1) Just One
-   Best use:   First game while everyone settles in.
-   How to explain in under 5 minutes:   One player guesses a secret word. Everyone else writes a one-word clue. Duplicate clues are removed before the guesser sees them.
-   Estimated play time:     20 minutes
-   Why it works:   Cooperative play keeps adults from overpowering the kids, and rounds move quickly.
Quick host tips
- Put the   10- and 12-year-old on different clue teams   so both stay engaged.
- Use   easier/common words   for the first 2 rounds.
- Remind everyone:   no phrases, no gestures, no “sounds like” clues  .
- Keep turns moving by giving clue writers about   20–30 seconds  .
2) Telestrations
-   Best use:   Middle game when energy is high.
-   How to explain in under 5 minutes:   Each player starts with a word, draws it, passes the sketch, next person guesses the drawing in words, and it keeps alternating until the booklet returns.
-   Estimated play time:     30 minutes
-   Why it works:   Great mix of adults and kids, lots of laughter, and no artistic skill needed.
Quick host tips
- If you have the full game, pick   family-friendly prompt cards  .
- Limit each drawing/guessing turn to about   60 seconds  .
- Encourage “funny is better than perfect” to reduce pressure.
- To keep mess low, use   erasable markers carefully   and keep a small cloth/tissue nearby.
3) Werewords Deluxe or One Night Ultimate Werewolf
-   Best use:   Final game, when everyone is ready for discussion and bluffing.
-   How to explain in under 5 minutes:
-   Werewords Deluxe:   Players ask yes/no questions to guess the secret word, but one hidden player is trying to mislead the group.
-   One Night Ultimate Werewolf:   Each player has a hidden role, a short night action may occur, then everyone debates and votes.
-   Estimated play time:     35 minutes
-   Why it works:   It adds suspense and conversation without needing a long campaign-style rules teach.
Quick host tips
-   Best pick for this mixed-age group: Werewords Deluxe   if you want smoother play and less social pressure.
-   Best pick for more bluffing:   One Night Ultimate Werewolf.
- For kids, avoid overly tricky role mixes at first; use the   simplest role set  .
- Keep each discussion round to   3–4 minutes max   so energy stays up.
- If anyone dislikes direct deception, choose   Werewords Deluxe   over Werewolf.
Best Fit for Your Group
If you want the smoothest 90-minute night, use this exact sequence:
-   0:20–0:50 — Telestrations
-   0:50–1:25 — Werewords Deluxe
-   1:25–1:30 — Quick favorite-moment vote / cleanup
This version is strongest because:
-   Just One   is the easiest opener
-   Telestrations   is the biggest laugh generator
-   Werewords Deluxe   gives you deduction without making the kids feel put on the spot too hard
Quick Actions
Option 1:   Most balanced lineup     Just One + Telestrations + Werewords Deluxe   Best for mixed ages
View Just One
Option 2:   More bluff-heavy finale     Just One + Telestrations + One Night Ultimate Werewolf   Best for louder groups
View Werewolf
Option 3:   Drawing-focused backup     If Telestrations is unavailable, use Fake Artist Goes to New York   Fast, funny, low mess
